column3: NKJV has “two of his disciples,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “sent through his disciples.”
Close to the Greek; “are evangelized” is rendered “have the gospel preached to them.”
Close to the Greek; “fall away” is rendered “is offended.”
NKJV has “ears to hear,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “ears.”
NKJV has “their companions,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the others.”
NKJV has “her children,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads ἔργων (“deeds”). “Drunkard” is rendered “winebibber.”
Close to the Greek; “miracles” is rendered “mighty works.”
NKJV follows the Textus Receptus: “who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades”; the critical text has a question, “Will you be exalted to heaven? You will go down to Hades.”
Close to the Greek; “I fully consent to You” (or “I praise You”) is rendered “I thank You,” and “little children” as “babes.”
